name: King of Moab
overview: The King of Moab was a male Moabite ruler during the time of the Exodus. He is noted specifically as the former king from whom Sihon, king of the Amorites, had taken land. This situates him within the broader narrative of territorial conflicts in the wilderness period of Israel's journey.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Moab' simply denotes his position as the monarch of the Moabite people. The name means 'king [of] Moab' and is a straightforward title rather than a personal name, indicating his role rather than individual identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this person beyond what is listed in his unique attribute. There are no known genealogical or relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Moab's significance lies in his connection to the territorial changes during the Exodus. His land was taken by Sihon, highlighting the shifting control of regions surrounding Israel as they journeyed to the Promised Land. This detail contributes to understanding the geopolitical landscape Israel encountered and the fulfillment of God's guidance in their conquest and settlement.
